'''Santana Terrell Moss''' (born June 1, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors.  Moss was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the first round of the [[2001 NFL draft]], where he spent four seasons with the team, before playing for the [[Washington Redskins]] for 10 seasons. Moss was selected as an [[All-Pro]] in 2005.

'''Saverio Giovanni Rocca''' (born 20 November 1973) is an Australian former professional sportsman. He played [[Australian rules football]] for [[Collingwood Football Club|Collingwood]] and the [[North Melbourne Football Club|Kangaroos]] in the [[Australian Football League]] (AFL), and then switched to playing [[American football]] as a [[Punter (American football)|punter]] for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[Washington Commanders|Washington Redskins]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Rocca was born in [[Melbourne]]. From 1992 to 2006, he played 257 AFL games as a [[full forward]] or [[centre half-forward]], kicking 748 goals. He ranks seventeenth on the [[List of VFL/AFL players to have scored 500 goals|all-time goalscoring list]]. Rocca was his team's leading goalkicker on ten occasions (seven for Collingwood and three for the Kangaroos), and in 1995 won the [[Copeland Trophy]] as Collingwood's [[best and fairest]] player. Only two players ([[Matthew Richardson (footballer)|Matthew Richardson]] and [[Kevin Bartlett (Australian rules footballer)|Kevin Bartlett]]) have scored more goals in their career without winning a [[Coleman Medal]] (i.e., scoring the most goals in a particular season).

Known for his ability to kick long distances, Rocca retired from Australian football at the age of 32 to pursue a career in the NFL. When he signed with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2007, he became the oldest rookie in the history of the NFL (breaking the record set by another Australian, [[Ben Graham (footballer)|Ben Graham]]).<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 September 2007 |title=Philadelphia Eagles punt on Old Rocca |url=http://www.worldfootynews.com/article.php/20070901143129215 |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=World Footy News}}</ref> After four seasons with the Eagles, Rocca joined the Washington Redskins in 2011, where he played three seasons through 2014. He then returned to Australia after the end of his NFL career, and worked as a kicking and ruck coach for the [[Carlton Football Club]] from 2015 to 2020.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-09-14 |title=Sav Rocca {{!}} LinkedIn |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/sav-rocca-725a114/?originalSubdomain=au |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230913222129/https://www.linkedin.com/in/sav-rocca-725a114/?originalSubdomain=au |archive-date=2023-09-13 |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=[[LinkedIn]]}}</ref>

He was selected 132nd overall by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the fifth round of the [[1992 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1992 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1992/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He won the 1992 [[NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year]] with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as he registered 10 [[quarterback sack|sacks]] and then played in two [[Super Bowl]]s with the [[Green Bay Packers]]. '''Sammy White''' (born March 3, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for 10 seasons with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

After playing [[college football]] at [[Grambling State University]], White was selected in the second round of the [[1976 NFL draft]] by Minnesota, and won the [[Associated Press]] [[Offense (sports)|Offensive]] [[NFL Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] and [[UPI NFL-NFC Rookie of the Year]] awards in 1976. He was a two-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection in 1976 and 1977. In 128 career games, he totaled 393 receptions, 6,400 receiving yards, and 50 [[touchdown]]s.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WhitSa00.htm | title=Sammy White | publisher=Sports Reference LLC | work=pro-football-reference.com | access-date=26 July 2014}}</ref>

'''Sandy Vincent Durko''' (born August 29, 1948) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Durko played football at [[West Covina High School]] in [[West Covina, California]], leading the team to a 1965 CIF championship.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.westcovina.org/civica/press/display.asp?layout=1&Entry=133 |title=Press Release |accessdate=2014-01-31 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201213353/http://www.westcovina.org/civica/press/display.asp?layout=1&Entry=133 |archivedate=2014-02-01 }}</ref>

Durko played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] as a starting [[defensive back]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.patriots.com/alumni/index.cfm?ac=alumnibiosdetail&bio=13817|title=Official Website of the New England Patriots|date=18 December 2014|website=Archive.patriots.com|accessdate=18 May 2018}}</ref> In the 1968 USC-[[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] game, on the second play from scrimmage Durko intercepted a [[Joe Theismann]] pass and returned it for a touchdown in a game that ended in a 21–21 tie.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1081877/2/index.htm |title=Notre Dame built a pocket to stuff Simpson in and unveiled - 12.09.68 - SI Vault |access-date=2014-01-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203150125/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1081877/2/index.htm |archive-date=2014-02-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was selected in the sixth round (137th overall) of the [[1970 NFL draft]] by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref name="pro-football-reference.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DurkSa20.htm|title=Sandy Durko Stats - Pro-Football-Reference.com|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|accessdate=18 May 2018}}</ref>

He played in only one game in his rookie year of 1970, the Bengals' first year in the NFL after the AFL-NFL merger. In 1971, however, he saw significant playing time at free safety, playing in all 14 games with four interceptions returned for a total of 46 yards. He also returned six punts for 14 yards and even rushed once for seven yards.<ref name="pro-football-reference.com"/>

In 1973, he joined the [[New England Patriots]] and started in all of the Patriots' 14 games, picking off three passes. He also returned three punts for 21 yards. The following year, 1974, was his fourth and final NFL season, as Durko played 11 games and started four for the Patriots.<ref name="pro-football-reference.com"/>

In 2011, he was one of 12 honorees inducted into the West Covina Walk of Fame, which "honors athletes, coaches and sports volunteers from the city who have made significant contributions in making West Covina a better place to live, work and play.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sgvtribune.com/general-news/20111119/west-covina-sports-figures-honored-at-walk-of-fame |title=West Covina sports figures honored at Walk of Fame |access-date=2014-01-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203123102/http://www.sgvtribune.com/general-news/20111119/west-covina-sports-figures-honored-at-walk-of-fame |archive-date=2014-02-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Durko is currently an investment management professional in [[Los Angeles]].<ref>[http://www.linkedin.com/profile/view?id=27011367&authType=NAME_SEARCH&authToken=c58_&locale=en_US&srchid=351454501391207072668&srchindex=1&srchtotal=2&trk=vsrp_people_res_name&trkInfo=VSRPsearchId%3A351454501391207072668%2CVSRPtargetId%3A27011367%2CVSRPcmpt%3Aprimary] {{dead link|date=May 2018}}</ref>
